# Introduction

Universities are experimenting with generative AI in writing courses while instructors and
students negotiate new expectations for feedback, authorship, and disclosure. This draft
reports what a small synthetic evidence set can and cannot support about structured
AI-assisted feedback in introductory writing courses.

# Method

The corpus is the four synthetic source summaries supplied with this task. Each summary
reports its own scope and limits. No external literature was consulted, and no causal
inference is available from these records.

# Findings

Structured AI prompting coincided with more visible outline revisions in one first-year
writing course [1] <!--ref:syn-classroom-01--><!--anchor:quote:Students%20using%20structured%20AI%20prompts%20produced%20more%20outline%20revisions%2C%20while%20final%20rubric%20scores%20varied%20widely-->.

Instructors reported faster formative feedback but additional time spent checking
unsupported claims [2] <!--ref:syn-interview-02--><!--anchor:quote:Instructors%20reported%20faster%20formative%20feedback%20but%20additional%20time%20spent%20checking%20unsupported%20claims-->.

Respondents valued rapid feedback, and some reported uncertainty about permitted use and
attribution [3] <!--ref:syn-survey-03--><!--anchor:quote:some%20reported%20uncertainty%20about%20permitted%20use%20and%20attribution-->.

Course-level disclosure rules are required, but acceptable assistance is left to instructors
[4] <!--ref:syn-policy-04--><!--anchor:quote:Course-level%20disclosure%20rules%20are%20required%2C%20but%20acceptable%20assistance%20is%20left%20to%20instructors-->.

# Limitations

- One course, no comparison group, and no validated measure of writing improvement
  [1] <!--ref:syn-classroom-01--><!--anchor:quote:No%20comparison%20group-->
  <!--anchor:quote:No%20validated%20measure%20of%20writing%20improvement-->.
- Instructor workload is self-reported and unmeasured
  [2] <!--ref:syn-interview-02--><!--anchor:quote:Self-reported%20workload-->.
- The survey is a voluntary response sample
  [3] <!--ref:syn-survey-03--><!--anchor:quote:Voluntary%20response%20bias-->.
- Policy text does not show implementation quality
  [4] <!--ref:syn-policy-04--><!--anchor:quote:Policy%20text%20does%20not%20show%20implementation%20quality-->.

# Conclusion

The supplied corpus supports a bounded description of revision activity and a visible
feedback-versus-verification trade-off. It does not support a workload reduction claim, and
it does not support a causal statement about policy clarity. Any narrowing of these
conclusions requires the author's confirmation.
